routes.label: Compare chords on the unit circle

question: What is the sum of all possible values of \(t\) between \(0\) and \(360\) such that the triangle in the coordinate plane whose vertices are \((\cos 40^\circ, \sin 40^\circ),\ \) \((\cos 60^\circ, \sin 60^\circ),\) and \(\ \ (\cos t^\circ, \sin t^\circ)\) is isosceles?
solution:
The coordinates describe points on the unit circle, so equal side lengths can be recognized through equal angular separations.

Call the points at angles \(40^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), and \(t^\circ\) respectively \(A,B,C\). The chord \(AB\) subtends a \(20^\circ\) central angle. Equal chords have equal smaller central angles, so we can examine every possible pair of equal sides:

| Equal sides | Valid values of \(t\) | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| \(AB=AC\) | \(20\) | The point \(C\) must be \(20^\circ\) from \(A\), giving \(t=20\) or \(60\). The latter repeats \(B\). |
| \(AB=BC\) | \(80\) | The point \(C\) must be \(20^\circ\) from \(B\), giving \(t=40\) or \(80\). The former repeats \(A\). |
| \(AC=BC\) | \(50,230\) | The point \(C\) lies on the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\). |

For the last row, the perpendicular bisector passes through the circle's center and the midpoint of the short arc from \(A\) to \(B\). That midpoint has angle
\[
\frac{40^\circ+60^\circ}{2}=50^\circ.
\]
The other intersection is diametrically opposite, at \(50^\circ+180^\circ=230^\circ\).

Every isosceles triangle has one of the three equal-side pairs listed. The four retained values are distinct and give three distinct points on the circle, so they form genuine triangles. Their sum is
\[
20+80+50+230=\boxed{380},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
